rules.exo: Exogenous policy rate (Norges Bank's published path, then constant)
rules.flx: FLX rule: R = π̄ + r̄r + 1.5(Δ₄pu − π̄) + 0.5(Δ₄y − ḡ)  (ABE2005 Table 1, ρ = 0)
rules.sm: SM rule: R = 0.75R₋₁ + 0.25(π̄ + r̄r) + 1.5(Δ₄pu − π̄) + 0.5(Δ₄y − ḡ)  (ABE2005 Table 1, ρ = 0.75)

ragged.note: Monthly series (CPI, CPI-ATE, I-44, rates) already observed for quarters after the national-accounts origin.

tracking.note: Deterministic dynamic simulation from the start quarter with every exogenous variable and the policy rate at their actual values; no residuals added back, so the paths show how far the system drifts from the data on its own dynamics (BJN2003 Figure 7, NAM2026 §2.3 practice).

bands.note: 500 bootstrap replications: residual vectors of the eight estimated equations resampled by quarter (keeping their cross-equation correlation) and added to the forecast quarters; 5–95% and 25–75% ranges of the resulting paths. Coefficient uncertainty is not included (NAM2026 reports 90% bands from stochastic simulation).

loss.note: 500 stochastic simulations of 24 quarters from the origin under each policy-rate setting, with identical residual draws (the eight equations' residual vectors resampled by quarter) so that the rules face the same shocks. V[·] is the variance pooled over quarters and draws, as in the counterfactual simulations of ABE2005 eq (10); the mean squared deviation of CPI-ATE inflation from the target is given beside it because the variance ignores a biased path. Coefficient uncertainty is not included.

ustar.note: u* is the unemployment rate at which the imposed wage curve and price mark-up hold together, given the actual wedge between consumer and import prices and the actual tax rates; the constants of the two long-run relations are the steady-state values of the EqCM terms implied by the estimated wage and price equations with inflation on target and productivity growing at the assumed rate. It is not an estimate of a NAIRU: in this model the equilibrium rate moves with the real exchange rate and the terms of trade (BJN2003 §2.3; Bårdsen, Eitrheim, Jansen and Nymoen 2005, ch. 6).

bands.note: Coefficient uncertainty, exogenous-rate case: 1000 draws of every estimated equation's coefficients from its OLS sampling distribution (Cholesky factor of the covariance; imposed long-run coefficients fixed; draws independent across equations), each draw simulated with and without the shock; 25–75% and 5–95% ranges of the differences. Residual resampling would give no width here because the system is linear in logs. The outer range is heavy-tailed: a few draws have near-unstable dynamics, so the interquartile range is the robust reading.

shock.note: Permanent +100 bp to the policy rate from the first forecast quarter (exogenous case) or to the rule's intercept (FLX, SM), shown as differences from the baseline path; the system is linear in logs, so the multipliers do not depend on the baseline. Published comparators: BJN2003 §6.1 (a permanent +1 point in RS lowers annual inflation by about 0.4 point in the long run); BN2008 Figure 5 (impact appreciation about 3%, inflation multiplier approaching −1 point after four years).

nam.status: NAM is maintained by Nymoen and Bårdsen through Normetrics (ragnar.nymoen@normetrics.no); documentation re-issued 10 Oct 2025, 10 and 18 Mar, 8 Apr, 31 May, 2 Sep and 5 Oct 2026 (https://normetrics.no/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/NAMdocumentation.pdf, 2026 vintage ~330 endogenous variables, EViews; forecast example in the documentation has forecast origin 2025Q2/2025Q3 with 90% stochastic-simulation fan charts). The documentation refers to 'the normal published forecast horizons' and 'the published model forecast', but no NAM forecast tables are published on normetrics.no after the 2017 posts and the 2017-2019 KS/KLP reports. Forecasts are delivered to model users: LO (publishes LO/NAM forecasts in Samfunnsnotat konjunkturutsiktene, March and May 2026), NHO, KLP (pension assumptions), KS (municipal wages), Samfunnsøkonomisk Analyse (house-price reports), and Finanstilsynet (NAM-FT with a bank module, used for the baseline and stress scenarios in Finansielt utsyn / the annual bank stress test, incl. June 2026).

publications.source: LO Samfunnsnotat nr. 3/2026 'Konjunkturutsiktene' (LO Samfunnspolitisk avdeling; forecasts made with NAM, labelled 'LO/NAM mai 2026')
publications.assumptions: Brent oil 92 USD/bbl 2026, 80 in 2027, 77 in 2028 (March round: 61/62/63); I-44 kept at the average of 1-19 April 2026 over the whole horizon (-4.9% in 2026, -0.5% 2027, 0.0 2028; positive = weaker krone); policy rate: two hikes in 2026 then down towards 3.5% by end of horizon, in line with Norges Bank MPR 1/2026 path (average 4.2% in 2026 and 2027, 3.7% in 2028); public demand growth 1.5-2% p.a. incl. NATO 3.5%+1.5% defence target; euro-area inflation and trading-partner growth revised for the Iran-US war/Hormuz disruption

Brent 68 (2025), 61/62/63 USD 2026-2028; I-44 kept at average of 1-19 Feb 2026 (-3.5% 2026, -0.2% 2027, 0.0 2028); one 0.25 pp rate cut per year 2026-2028 (policy rate avg 3.9/3.7/3.4); public demand ~2% growth; SSB KT 4/2025 and Norges Bank PPR 4/2025 used for fiscal comparison

sim_inputs.note: Arrays start eight quarters before the origin (position 8) so that every lag the equations use is available.
